ingredients.name: Eggplant (long, slender variety)
ingredients.notes: about 2 medium eggplants, cut into thick strips or 1-inch cubes

ingredients.name: Turmeric powder
ingredients.notes: for coating the eggplant before frying

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: split: for the eggplant before frying, plus more to taste

ingredients.name: Oil for deep frying
ingredients.notes: approx. 2 cups; vegetable oil is more typical than coconut oil for the deep-frying step

ingredients.name: Shallots or pearl onions
ingredients.notes: peeled, left whole or halved if large

ingredients.name: Mustard seeds, ground
ingredients.notes: ground to a powder, or 1 tbsp whole mustard seeds blistered in oil first

ingredients.name: Vinegar (white or coconut vinegar)
ingredients.notes: about 1/3 cup; the souring agent that defines the dish

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: balances the vinegar's sourness; adjust to taste

ingredients.name: Maldive fish flakes
ingredients.notes: optional but adds traditional umami depth; omit for a vegetarian/vegan moju

steps.instruction: Cut the eggplant into thick, even strips or 1-inch cubes, sized consistently so they fry evenly.
Toss the eggplant with the turmeric and half the salt. Let sit for 10-15 minutes, then gently squeeze out any released liquid.

Heat the oil in a wok or deep pan until hot but not smoking. Fry the eggplant in small batches until deep golden brown on all sides, turning frequently. Drain well on paper towels or a clean cloth -- thorough draining keeps the moju from spoiling quickly.
In the same oil, quickly fry the shallots for about 30 seconds until lightly softened, then the green chillies for about a minute. Drain both on paper towels.
If using Maldive fish flakes, fry them briefly in the oil until crisp and golden, then drain.

In a bowl, combine the ground mustard, chilli powder, garlic, ginger, sugar, remaining salt, and vinegar. Mix until the sugar dissolves into a smooth sauce. Taste and adjust until sour, sweet, and salty flavours feel balanced.
Heat a tablespoon of the frying oil in a clean pan. Pour in the mustard-vinegar sauce and bring to a brief simmer, about a minute, to take the raw edge off the vinegar and mustard.
Add the fried eggplant, shallots, green chillies, curry leaves, and Maldive fish flakes (if using) to the simmering sauce. Stir well to coat everything evenly, and cook for about a minute more.

Remove from heat and let cool completely. For the best flavour, let the moju rest for at least a few hours, or ideally 1-2 days, before serving, allowing the eggplant to fully absorb the vinegar and mustard. Store in a clean, dry glass jar.

source_site: islandsmile.org, cross-checked against hungrylankan.com, notquitenigella.com, and themadscientistskitchen.com for technique and flavour-balance consistency
collection_method: scraped, cross-checked across 4 independent sources for consistent fry-then-pickle technique and the essential sweet-sour-salty balance
notes: Brinjal/wambatu moju is considered an essential component of any proper Sri Lankan rice-and-curry spread and a near-mandatory dish at weddings and festive events. Maldive fish flakes are traditional but optional; omitting them makes the dish fully vegan. The dish is not truly 'pickled' in the long-fermentation sense -- it is a quick vinegar-mustard relish that develops flavour over hours to a couple of days, and can keep at room temperature for about a week if the eggplant was fried and drained thoroughly, or longer if refrigerated. Some family recipes add ground cinnamon, cloves, and cardamom to the mustard-vinegar sauce for a more complex, warmly spiced version; this entry reflects the simpler, more common household version.
